methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.summary: Write `adapter_config.json` into `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
The file is the reference's: `to_dict` with its keys sorted,
indented by two spaces.  The directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
`auto_mapping_dict` replaces the `auto_mapping` the file records.
The reference forwards any other keyword to its hub upload; there
is no hub here, so another key raises.

raises.description: `save_directory` names an existing file.
`kwargs` holds a key other than `auto_mapping_dict`.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d).r
2

methods.name: from_json_file
methods.summary: Read a config file into the dict it holds, unchanged but for `runtime_config`.
methods.extended:
What `from_pretrained` reads before it chooses a config class: the
file's content as a dict, as the reference's `from_json_file` returns
it.  `from_dict` turns it into a config.

parameters.name: path_json_file
parameters.description: The path of a JSON file such as `adapter_config.json`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature; it passes none to the
reader, and any key given here raises.

returns.description:
The file's object, without a `runtime_config` key: the
reference warns that such a key is ignored, since a runtime
configuration is valid at runtime only.

raises.description: There is no file at `path_json_file`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.
`kwargs` is not empty.

examples:
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     raw = PeftConfig.from_json_file(os.path.join(d, "adapter_config.json"))
>>> raw["peft_type"], raw["r"]
('LORA', 2)

methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class: called on

parameters.description:
A directory under `pretrained_model_name_or_path` that holds

parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`,

methods.name: from_peft_type
methods.summary: Build a config from its fields given as keyword arguments, the class chosen by `peft_type`.
methods.extended:
The reference's way to turn the keys of a config file into a config: the
`peft_type` argument names the method and so the class, whichever class this is
called on.  Without one, the calling class is built.  The fields are read as
`from_dict` reads them, so a key this library has no field for is accepted
at a value that turns its feature off (dropped, with a warning when the key is
unknown), where the reference drops it at any value.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description: The config's fields, by name; `peft_type` is a `PeftType` or its string.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class `peft_type` names.

raises.description: `peft_type` names no method of this library.
No `peft_type` is given and this is `PeftConfig` itself, which builds no config of its own.
A key turns on a feature this library does not implement.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> config = PeftConfig.from_peft_type(peft_type="LORA", r=4, target_modules=["q"])
>>> type(config).__name__, config.r
('LoraConfig', 4)
>>> LoraConfig.from_peft_type(r=2, target_modules=["q"]).r
2

methods.name: check_kwargs
methods.summary: Check the fields about to build a config; the reference's hook for a class to refuse a file it cannot read.
methods.extended:
The reference calls it on the keys of an adapter file before building the config.
A config class overrides it to refuse or warn about a file written for an older
release of its method (`OFTConfig.check_kwargs`); the base accepts everything.
`from_pretrained` here does not call it.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description: The config's fields, by name.

returns.description: The fields to build the config with: `kwargs` itself.

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with LN tuning.
members.extended:
LN tuning (Zhao et al., 2023, [arXiv:2312.11420](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11420) — "Tuning LayerNorm in
Attention") trains the normalisation layers of a model and nothing else:
each targeted layer gets a copy of itself that trains while the original
stays frozen.  The method adds no tensor of its own, so it is a few
$d$ parameters per layer; "merging" makes the trained copy the layer.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference
adapter library's.  Unlike the reference's, this
config also takes `layers_to_transform` / `layers_pattern`, which select layers
the way `LoraConfig`'s do; `adapter_config.json` holds them only when they are
set, and `from_pretrained` reads files with or without them.

>>> LNTuningConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config

methods.signature: merge(safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Make an adapter's copy the layer's values, in place.
methods.extended:
One adapter can be merged at a time.  Asking for another while one is
merged unmerges the first, with a warning.

parameters.description: Check the tuned values for NaN / inf first and leave the base untouched if there are any.

The adapter is disabled.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Run the active adapter's trained copy of the layer.
methods.extended:
The original layer when adapters are disabled, every active adapter is merged or none
applies; more than one applied adapter raises `ValueError`, since LN tuning applies
one copy at a time.  The copy of an adapter does not hold what another's merge
exchanged into the base, so it runs whether or not one is merged.

methods.name: update_layer
methods.summary: Create adapter `adapter_name` from `config`.
methods.extended:
The adapter is built whole before the layer holds any of it.  A layer
that holds an adapter already keeps applying the adapters it applied:
the new one is inactive until `set_adapter` names it; a layer with
none starts applying this one.

parameters.description: Key of the adapter in each of the layer's tables.

parameters.description: The method's config.

One step down: where another tuner layer stands between, that layer, not the user's

members.extended:
The layer applies the copy of the one active adapter it holds; with none it
runs the base.  It wraps any module that takes and returns one tensor.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The module to tune; kept as `base_layer`, its parameters shared.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter created at once.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The adapter's config.

raises.description: `base_layer` builds parameters on its first input.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LNTuningConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.ln_tuning import LNTuningLayer
>>> base = nn.LayerNorm(4)
>>> layer = LNTuningLayer(base, "default", LNTuningConfig(target_modules=["x"]))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # the copy starts as the base
True
>>> layer.ln_tuning_layers["default"].weight is base.weight
False

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter starts frozen and inactive: the forward pass keeps
applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the
`requires_grad` it had.  `set_adapter` switches to it.  A
module an earlier adapter already wraps takes the new one beside
it; any other target is wrapped.  The model is left as it was if
the adapter cannot be added.

parameters.description: What to adapt and how — the config class of this tuner's method.

The name is taken or malformed, the config is another
method's, no module matches it, or it cannot sit beside the
adapters held (two adapters training biases).
`config` is not an adapter config.

methods.signature: set_adapter(adapter_name: str | list[str], inference_mode: bool = False)

Every other adapter is frozen; the activated ones train unless
`inference_mode`.  A merged layer is unmerged first.  Layers that
hold none of the named adapters run their base alone.  The
parameters `bias` makes trainable follow the adapter that asked
for them.

A name is not one of the model's adapters, or two named
adapters train the same `modules_to_save` module.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter: its parameters, its config, its `modules_to_save` copies.
methods.extended:
If it was active, the adapters still active stay so; when none
remain the first of the others (by name) takes over, with a
warning, and trains.  Deleting the last adapter leaves the layers
in the model, applying nothing; `unload()` removes them.

raises.description: The adapter does not exist, or it is merged — unmerge first.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the adapted model; its adapter layers do their work inside the call.

methods.name: merge_adapter
methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.
methods.extended:
A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

Merging some of the active adapters leaves the others applying: a merged
layer runs its folded weights and then the active adapters it has not
folded, so the model computes what it did unmerged.  The reference runs a
merged layer's base alone, which drops the others; Lucid departs from that
on purpose (LCD-971).  Merging an adapter that is not active adds it: the
layers then run the weights with it folded in and the active adapters they
have not folded (the base with that adapter alone, in the reference).  A
method whose adapters do not compute the same function once split refuses
it: those that apply in order (OFT, BOFT, HRA, RoAd's `road_2` and
`road_4`, MiSS / Bone's `bat`) take only the first of the active
adapters, in their order; a LoRA layer refuses to fold some adapters while
a DoRA one stays unmerged; LN tuning, which runs one adapter's copy at a
time, refuses to fold an active adapter while another is active.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description:
Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.  A layer holding
only some of them merges those.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or the adapter is
disabled (inside `disable_adapter()`).

A name is not one of the model's adapters, `safe_merge` found a
non-finite merged weight, or a layer's method cannot go on applying
the active adapters that stay unmerged.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4)), config)
>>> peft.add_adapter("two", config)
>>> peft.base_model.set_adapter(["default", "two"])
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> both = peft(x)
>>> peft.base_model.merge_adapter(adapter_names=["default"])
>>> peft.base_model.model[0].merged_adapters
['default']
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(peft(x), both, atol=1e-5))   # "two" still applies
True

methods.name: unmerge_adapter
methods.summary: Take every merged adapter update back out of its base weight.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Accepted for the reference's signature; there is no progress bar.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.

returns.description: The model, merged, with no adapter layer left in it.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

methods.name: enable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Apply the adapter again after `disable_adapter_layers`.

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Run the base model alone: adapter updates off, original `modules_to_save`.

methods.name: supports_lora_conversion
methods.summary: Whether every adapted layer in this tuner supports conversion to LoRA.

members.summary: A model whose chosen normalisation layers train as copies, and the tools to take them out again.
members.extended:
Each module `config` selects is replaced by an
`lucid.peft.tuners.ln_tuning.LNTuningLayer` around it — the module
and a trainable copy of it — and every other parameter is frozen.  The model
is changed in place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper lacks is
read from it.  `peft_config` holds a copy of `config` with the default
`target_modules` spelled out; `config` is untouched.

Any number of adapters live side by side, each under its own name, but only
one applies (and only one can be merged) at a time: see `add_adapter`,
`set_adapter` and `delete_adapter`.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `ln_tuning_layers`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

raises.description:
Nothing matches `target_modules`, the model type has no default
`target_modules` and the config names none, or `modules_to_save` matches nothing.
The model already holds adapter layers of another method.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LNTuningConfig, LNTuningModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.LayerNorm(8), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> tuned = LNTuningModel(net, LNTuningConfig(target_modules=["1"]), "default")
>>> tuned.targeted_module_names
['1']
>>> net[1].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[1].ln_tuning_layers["default"].weight.requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> tuned.unload() is net, type(net[1]) is nn.LayerNorm
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.ln_tuning` — LN tuning: train a copy of each chosen normalisation layer.
extended:
LN tuning (Zhao et al., 2023, [arXiv:2312.11420](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11420) — Tuning LayerNorm in Attention) trains the
normalisation layers of a model and nothing else.  Each chosen layer gets a copy of itself that
trains while the original stays frozen; the method adds no tensor of its own, so an adapter is a few
$d$ parameters per layer, and merging makes the trained copy the layer.  Pick it for a tiny
adapter that needs no new tensors.  It applies one adapter at a time.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, LNTuningLayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.ln_tuning import LNTuningConfig, LNTuningLayer` read as they do there.  One layer
type, which wraps whichever module `target_modules` names.  `LNTuningConfig` and
`LNTuningModel` are here and exported from `lucid.peft`.  Importing the package registers the
method (its config under `PeftType.LN_TUNING`, its tuner and layer), which is what makes
`get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Zhao, Bingchen, et al. "Tuning LayerNorm in Attention: Towards Efficient Multi-Modal LLM Finetuning." [arXiv:2312.11420](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11420), 2023.
theory:
LN tuning (Zhao et al., 2023, [arXiv:2312.11420](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11420) — "Tuning LayerNorm in
Attention") trains the normalisation layers of a model and nothing else:
each targeted layer gets a copy of itself that trains while the original
stays frozen.  The method adds no tensor of its own, so it is a few
$d$ parameters per layer; "merging" makes the trained copy the layer.
